text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.5% today after climbing sharply over the prior three trading days, giving back some recent gains. The move comes as crude oil prices dipped (US oil at $89.62/barrel today) and Russian crude production has rebounded to surplus levels globally, which typically pressures refiner margins—the spread between what refiners pay for oil and what they sell refined products for. Even though refineries are running at a healthy 95.2% capacity, rising global supply without matching demand growth squeezes profitability.

The broader headwind is a shift in market sentiment on energy supply. After weeks of tighter markets that benefited refiners, the International Energy Agency reported this week that Russia's oil exports are recovering and global supply now exceeds demand. That surplus dynamic—even with heating oil prices up sharply year-over-year—tends to weigh on refiner stocks regardless of near-term inventory levels or utilization rates.
